content.title: About
content.content: Steak tartare is a dish of raw ground beef seasoned with spices, onion, capers, mustard and Worcestershire sauce. It is traditionally served with a raw egg yolk, toast points or potato chips. Preparation requires only the freshest, high‑quality meat that has passed strict safety checks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tartare originated in early 19th‑century Paris as a dish for raw‑meat enthusiasts.
The name derives from the Turkic‑Tatar nomads who ate raw meat, though the modern recipe is quite different.
The original recipe used only beef tenderloin, without any egg.
Tartare is often served in fine‑dining restaurants where meat quality and seasoning precision are paramount.
In some countries the dish is called "carpaccio," although carpaccio is usually thinly sliced rather than minced.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat is a good source of heme iron and zinc, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tartare contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 content when using grass‑fed beef
items.content: Meat from grass‑fed cattle is richer in beneficial omega‑3 fatty acids.

items.title: Risk of foodborne infection
items.content: Raw meat can harbor pathogenic bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella). Use only fresh, inspected meat and keep it below 4 °C.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Seasonings such as Worcestershire or soy sauce can significantly increase the salt level.

items.title: Not suitable for pregnant women and immunocompromised persons
items.content: Raw meat is not recommended for those at increased risk of infection.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tartare immediately after preparation on a chilled plate. Eat with a spoon, pairing it with toast points, crispy bread, potato chips or fresh vegetables. Add the egg yolk to taste for extra creaminess.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the ground beef in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and use within 24 hours. Ensure the meat has no off‑odor or discoloration before serving. If freezing, store in an airtight container and consume within 1‑2 months.
